oi.text: The Company’s primary financial measure for evaluating each of its apartment communities is net operating income (“NOI”). NOI represents rental income less direct property operating expenses (including real estate taxes and insurance). The Company believes that NOI is helpful to investors as a supplemental measure of its operating performance because it is a direct measure of the actual operating results of the Company’s apartment properties.

oi.text: Our primary financial measure for evaluating each of our apartment communities is net operating income (“NOI”). NOI represents rental income less direct property operating expenses (including property taxes). Management considers NOI to be an important and appropriate supplemental performance measure to net income because it helps both investors and management to understand the core operations of a community or communities prior to the allocation of any corporate-level property management overhead or financing-related costs. Residential NOI represents results attributable to our apartment rental operations, including parking and other ancillary residential revenue.

nonop.text: Interest expense increased $55.6 million, or 81.6%, and $70.7 million, or 35.7%, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to the prior year periods, primarily resulting from the Merger, whereby the Company assumed $8.4 billion principal amount of secured and unsecured indebtedness that remained outstanding as of September 30, 2026. The debt assumed in the Merger was recognized at fair value, resulting in a net discount of $516.0 million, which is recognized as an increase to the contractual interest expense over the life of the related debt. The increase in interest expense was partially offset by higher capitalized interest. The Company capitalized interest of $17.9 million and $13.7 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $48.4 million and $36.1 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

net.text: Net loss attributable to Common Shares for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $735.5 million compared to net income attributable to Common Shares of $381.3 million for the prior year period, a decrease of $1.1 billion. The decrease was primarily attributable to an increase in depreciation expense driven by real estate assets acquired in the Merger, specifically in-place lease intangible assets, and transaction costs associated with the Merger.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Cash flows from operations are determined by operating activities and factors including but not limited to (i) the number of apartment homes owned, (ii) rental rates, (iii) occupancy levels, (iv) uncollectible lease revenue levels or interruptions in collections caused by market conditions, (v) operating expenses and (vi) capital expenditures with respect to our communities. Cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the prior year period decreased by $228.8 million primarily due to the payment of Merger-related costs and an increase in prepaid expenses and other assets.

da.text: Depreciation increased $667.6 million to $898.0 million and $684.1 million to $1.4 billion, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to the prior year periods, primarily due to expense recognized in the current-year periods on in-place lease intangible assets and real estate acquired in the Merger.

wc.text: We generally expect to meet our short-term liquidity requirements, including capital expenditures related to maintaining our existing communities and scheduled unsecured note and mortgage note repayments, through our working capital, net cash provided by operating activities and borrowings under our Unsecured Revolving Credit Facilities and Commercial Paper Program (each as defined below). We consider these sources of liquidity to be adequate to meet operating requirements and payments of distributions.

intro.text: Equity Residential (“EQR”) is committed to creating communities where people thrive. The Company, a member of the S&P 500, owns and manages rental properties in dynamic metro areas across the U.S. ERP Operating Limited Partnership (“ERPOP”) is focused on conducting the multifamily property business of EQR. EQR is a Maryland real estate investment trust (“REIT”) formed in March 1993 and ERPOP is an Illinois limited partnership formed in May 1993. References to the “Company,” “we,” “us” or “our” mean collectively EQR, ERPOP and those entities/subsidiaries owned or controlled by EQR and/or ERPOP. References to the “Operating Partnership” mean collectively ERPOP and those entities/subsidiaries owned or controlled by ERPOP.
